Denmark’s oldest-ever person was a member of the Danish Nazi party
Records show that 112-year-old Kirsten Schwalbe joined Denmark’s Nazi party during the German occupation. She says she did so at her husband’s request and did not sympathise with Nazism.
Kirsten Schwalbe, who this week became the longest-living Dane in recorded history, was a member of Denmark’s Nazi party during the German occupation.
The 112-year-old joined the National Socialist Workers’ Party of Denmark (DNSAP) in August 1941, according to Kristeligt Dagblad.
Her name appears in the Bovrup registry, a record of people who were members of DNSAP. Two historians have independently confirmed to the newspaper that the entry matches Schwalbe’s date of birth and address, although her surname is misspelled as “Schalbe”.
Schwalbe has confirmed that both she and her former husband were members of the party, but says she only joined because her husband urged her to do so.
She rejected the suggestion that she had sided with Nazi Germany.
“Not at all. I barely knew what it was, because I have never taken an interest in politics,” she told TV Midtvest when asked whether she had sympathised with the Nazis.
Schwalbe said she found it unfair that she should have to “pay for it” more than 70 years later, adding that “back then, wives didn’t look into such things”.
Membership does not show level of involvement
DNSAP was founded in 1930 and was strongly inspired by Adolf Hitler’s German Nazi Party, the NSDAP.
But Charlie Krautwald, a historian at the University of Copenhagen, cautioned against drawing conclusions about Schwalbe’s level of involvement from the registry alone.
The record shows that a person joined the party, he told Kristeligt Dagblad, but not why they joined, how long they remained a member or whether they paid membership fees.
A person could therefore appear in the registry without having been active in the party.
TV Midtvest has followed Schwalbe for several years and manages an Instagram account about her life. Two of the broadcaster’s employees have also recently published a book about her.
Her membership of DNSAP had not previously been mentioned. TV Midtvest editor-in-chief Marc Killigren Akselsen told Kristeligt Dagblad that the broadcaster had not known about it.
Schwalbe, who lives in Struer in western Jutland, became the longest-living Dane on record on Wednesday, when she reached the age of 112 years and 218 days.

Lidl has Denmark’s cheapest basket of organic groceries, analysis finds
Lidl offers the lowest prices on a selected basket of organic groceries among seven Danish supermarket chains, according to an analysis by price-monitoring service Madprisluppen.
A basket containing 22 organic products cost 355.20 DKK at Lidl. The same basket cost 449.60 DKK at Meny, the most expensive chain in the comparison.
Madprisluppen said the Lidl basket was 26 percent cheaper than the one at Meny.
“We want to make it easier for Danes to make room for organics in everyday life, and here price plays an important role,” Lidl Denmark purchasing director Peer Sandtner said.
Rema 1000 was the second-cheapest supermarket, with its basket costing only 5 DKK more than Lidl’s.
SuperBrugsen was the second-most expensive, though its total was almost 35 DKK below Meny’s.
The analysis also included Netto, 365discount and Føtex. Prices were recorded from October 9 through October 12.
Products included milk, eggs, vegetables and dry goods. Meat was excluded because Madprisluppen found it difficult to identify comparable products across the chains.
The monitoring service also found that supermarkets carry fewer organic products than they did six years ago. Organic prices have increased, and such products appear in special offers less frequently than non-organic groceries.
Norway to lend 10-meter Viking boat to Danish museum for 10 years
A Norwegian Viking boat will be displayed at Moesgaard Museum near Aarhus under an unusual 10-year loan agreement.
The oak boat is almost 10 meters long and nearly two meters wide. It was among three smaller vessels discovered when archaeologists excavated Norway’s Gokstad ship in 1880.
The Gokstad ship is Norway’s largest preserved Viking ship.
“The boat is a very important cultural treasure from the Viking Age, and it is not an everyday occurrence that we grant permission for such a boat to be taken out of the country,” Kaare Stang of Riksantikvaren, Norway’s cultural heritage authority, said.
The three smaller boats had been chopped into pieces, possibly as part of a burial ritual, according to archaeologists.
The Museum of Cultural History in Norway owns the boat and applied for permission to lend it to Moesgaard Museum for a new exhibition.
Norwegian authorities normally approve loans for no more than three years. Moesgaard Museum must therefore submit a report on the boat’s condition every three years during the loan period.
Stang said Norwegian authorities trusted the Danish museum to protect the boat but emphasized that it must eventually return to Norway.
No arrival date has been announced.
Moesgaard Museum already displays a 6.5-meter Gokstad boat that was used to transport crews and exchange orders between warships.
Copenhagen establishes support groups for parents of children missing school
A new parents’ association has signed a four-year agreement with the City of Copenhagen to establish support groups for families whose children experience prolonged, involuntary school absence.
Such absence is often connected to poor well-being and is considered concerning when a pupil misses at least 20 percent of school for two consecutive quarters. That corresponds to about 10 days per quarter.
The first groups will be funded by Copenhagen and include eight to nine parents who meet approximately once a month, education news outlet Folkeskolen.dk reported.
A family therapist will lead the meetings, with a parent from Forældrekommissionen, or the Parents’ Commission, also participating.
Louise Gielov and Jens Langorn helped establish the association after their family appeared in the Danish public broadcaster DR documentary “Skolens tabte børn,” which showed daily life with children unable to attend school.
The couple received more than 1,000 messages from parents in similar situations after the documentary aired.
The association now has 2,545 members and aims to establish parent groups across Denmark. It also plans to use families’ experiences to promote earlier intervention and broader changes to prevent school absence.
The proportion of pupils with prolonged concerning absence increased from 2.4 percent in the 2019-2020 school year to 5.1 percent in 2024-2025.
The association has also secured 7 million DKK from foundations.
Dane becomes first European participant to receive combined flu and Covid vaccine
A 65-year-old Dane will become the first person in Europe to receive a new combined influenza and Covid-19 vaccine as part of a clinical trial Friday.
The trial will examine whether one injection can protect against both diseases as effectively as, or better than, the two separate vaccines currently used, Danish public broadcaster DR reported.
The first participant will receive the vaccine at Gentofte Hospital.
“We are investigating whether one shot with this new vaccine is just as effective or potentially better than the two shots given today at preventing hospitalizations with influenza and Covid-19,” said Tor Biering-Sørensen, a professor and senior physician at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital who is leading the trial.
About 165,000 Danes have agreed to participate. More than 300,000 people are expected to join over the next two years.
Half of the participants will receive one dose of the combined vaccine. The other half will receive separate influenza and Covid-19 vaccinations.
People age 65 and older in Denmark are automatically invited to receive free vaccinations against both diseases. The Danish Health Authority said about 1.3 million residents received invitations in September.
People with chronic illnesses or other conditions placing them at increased risk are also eligible for the free program.

Archaeologists uncover more than 1,000 graves in Copenhagen park
Archaeologists have excavated more than 1,000 graves containing human remains beneath Hans Tavsens Park in Copenhagen’s Nørrebro district.
The park, located next to Assistens Cemetery, was previously used as a burial ground for Copenhagen’s poorest residents. Victims of the city’s 1853 cholera epidemic are among those buried there.
“We can use it to gain insight into the poor population from this period and Copenhagen’s history,” Museum of Copenhagen archaeologist Olivia Persson told Danish public broadcaster DR.
The excavation is taking place before Hans Tavsens Park and the neighboring Hans Tavsens Gade are redeveloped into a connected green space.
The project will also allow the park to collect water during cloudbursts, helping prevent flooding of nearby roads and basements as Denmark experiences wetter weather.
Construction began in autumn 2025 as part of the City of Copenhagen’s plan for managing extreme rainfall. The redevelopment is expected to be completed in spring 2028.
Most of the remains will be transferred to the University of Copenhagen’s Anthropological Laboratory for storage and examination. Some will undergo additional analysis, while the remainder will be reburied in the park.
Researchers will examine the health of selected individuals. They will also study how the graves were arranged to better understand religious and cultural attitudes toward death among Copenhagen’s poorer population at the time.

Greenland’s parliament unanimously adopted a resolution Thursday directing the government to draft legislation temporarily banning deep-sea mining.
The proposed ban would remain in effect through December 31, 2029, with the possibility of two-year extensions.
Naalakkersuisut, Greenland’s government, supported the considerations behind the resolution. It said it would introduce a bill for the temporary ban during parliament’s spring 2027 session.
The ban must therefore pass as legislation before taking effect.
WWF Greenland, the local branch of the World Wide Fund for Nature, called the decision “an important step in the right direction,” according to AFP.
“With this decision, Greenland has the opportunity to send a strong signal that the protection of the ocean, nature and the Greenlanders’ livelihood must be taken seriously when we face new forms of exploitation of marine resources,” the organization said.
WWF Greenland says deep-sea mining can damage marine ecosystems and biodiversity.
Fishing is the main driver of Greenland’s economy, while hunting remains important to local communities.
The vote came one day after US President Donald Trump said oil, gas and mineral exploration was beginning in Greenland. Greenland’s government subsequently denied the claim. Trump did not mention deep-sea mining.
Greenland suspended new oil and gas exploration permits in 2021. Industrial oil drilling and gas extraction have never been conducted there, according to AFP.
Denmark considers lower temperature rule to allow electric cremation ovens
Denmark’s 20 crematoria could replace oil- and gas-powered ovens with electric models if authorities approve a lower minimum temperature requirement.
The Danish Environmental Protection Agency has proposed reducing the required temperature in cremation ovens’ post-combustion chambers from 800 to 750 degrees Celsius, engineering publication Ingeniøren reported.
The proposed change has been submitted for public consultation.
Electric ovens are expected to reduce both environmental effects and the financial cost of cremations.
Michael Smidemann, chair of the Danish Crematoria Association, said crematoria were interested in replacing their existing ovens.
“The background is a desire to sharpen the green profile, even though it is somewhat mixed how green the electricity we receive actually is,” he told Ingeniøren.
Electric cremation ovens can reach 750 degrees. Requiring them to reach 800 degrees would demand additional heating elements, increasing electricity use and causing heavy wear on the ovens’ brickwork, according to Ingeniøren.
Denmark recorded 58,185 deaths in 2025, according to the Danish Crematoria Association.
Of those who died, 51,252 were cremated, corresponding to 88.1 percent of all deaths.
A cremation typically takes about 90 minutes, according to information from the City of Copenhagen and other sources.
Specialized services received 61 percent of growth in municipal spending
Denmark’s specialized social and education services received 61 percent of the inflation-adjusted growth in municipal service spending from 2018 through 2025.
The finding comes from an analysis by Arbejderbevægelsens Erhvervsråd, or AE, an economic policy institute linked to the Danish labor movement, according to Dagbladet Information.
Specialized services include support for children, young people and adults with particular needs, along with special classes and special education.
Municipalities spent approximately 80 billion DKK on these areas in 2018. By 2025, spending had risen to 93 billion DKK.
Residential facilities accounted for 40 percent of the increase. Municipal spending on those facilities now totals about 27 billion DKK, according to AE.
“When expenditures in the specialized areas grow, there is less money for the general areas, which also need investments,” AE director Lars Andersen said.
However, the analysis does not establish that the increased specialized spending directly caused cuts elsewhere.
Municipal service funding also covers daycare centers, public schools and elderly care.
The government and Local Government Denmark, the association representing Denmark’s municipalities, have increased the overall spending limit annually since 2018. Their latest agreement raises it by 3.3 billion DKK for 2027.
Finance Minister Peter Hummelgaard of the Social Democrats has previously acknowledged that rapidly rising specialized social service costs continue to create financial difficulties for some municipalities.

Through its existing model, retailers sell unsold food in discounted surprise bags, with Too Good To Go receiving a percentage of each transaction.
The company says its expansion will help businesses recover value from unsold merchandise while giving customers access to a wider selection of discounted products.
“Our partners are increasingly approaching us with challenges regarding surplus goods that extend beyond food and asking if we can help. Surplus exists in all parts of the store,” Lykke said.
Surplus stock can include seasonal products, discontinued items, outdated packaging and gift sets that are no longer in demand.

Tiny parasitic wasp discovered in Denmark for the first time
A nature enthusiast searching beneath ferns in a North Zealand forest has identified an insect species never previously recorded in the country.
The discovery was made in mid-September at Gribskov National Nature Park during a bioblitz, a 24-hour event in which participants search for and document wildlife.
Around 70 people took part in the event, organized in collaboration with the Vores Vilde Natur project and biodiversity platform Arter.dk.
Nature educator Lars Holm Hansen discovered the wasp, measuring just a few millimeters, while shaking bracken ferns to examine the insects hiding underneath.
He collected several specimens using an insect aspirator but could not immediately identify them.
After posting a photograph on Arter.dk, he received help from experts who identified the species as Hemiptarsenus ornatus.
“It shows that if you put in a little effort out in the field, you can get lucky, and it is simply worth the effort,” Hansen said.
The Natural History Museum of Denmark confirmed the finding in a press release.
Museum insect curator Lars Vilhelmsen explained that the species has previously been recorded in Germany, Sweden and Norway.
“It has probably been here all along. It is already known from several countries around us, but it is so small that you do not just easily spot it,” Vilhelmsen said.
He added that relatively few people in Denmark study parasitic wasps, meaning many species may remain undocumented.
Hansen, who had participated in six bioblitz events this year, also suggested the insect’s Danish name: smykket dværgsnyltehveps.
He believes Danish names make unfamiliar species easier to discuss and remember.

The charges in the North Zealand case have been brought under that provision, with the defendants’ criminal responsibility yet to be established.

Denmark’s National Special Crime Unit, known as NSK, told Kristeligt Dagblad that it could not determine what proportion of child sexual abuse material involved artificial intelligence.

Three Danish films shortlisted for Europe’s Oscars
Three Danish films have been shortlisted for the European Film Awards, often described as Europe’s equivalent of the Oscars.
The films are the dramas Kvinde ukendt by May el-Toukhy and Gæsten by Mads Mengel, and Sine Plambech’s documentary Rescue, the Danish Film Institute announced on Instagram.
A total of 45 films have been shortlisted in the fiction category.
May el-Toukhy’s Kvinde ukendt has already received international recognition. The drama was selected for the Venice Film Festival in September, where it won the main prize, the Golden Lion. Its lead actress, Mathilde Arcel, was named best actress.
The film has also been selected as Denmark’s entry for the Academy Awards in the Best International Feature Film category.
Set during the liberation of Denmark in May 1945, the drama follows a woman who has worked as a maid in the home of an elderly, respected widower she is now preparing to marry. She struggles to hide the fact that she has had a relationship with a German soldier.
Mads Mengel’s Gæsten has also attracted international attention. In July, the film received two awards at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival in the Czech Republic.
It won the Special Jury Prize in the festival’s main competition, known as the Crystal Globe Competition, while Mengel was named best director.
The film follows Karl and Emilie, a couple preparing to host a naming ceremony for their son. Their plans are disrupted when an uninvited guest arrives: Karl’s mother, played by Trine Dyrholm, with whom he has not spoken for years.
The third Danish film on the shortlist is Rescue, a documentary by anthropologist Sine Plambech. It had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.
The documentary follows people fleeing across the Mediterranean and examines how the European Union’s border policies affect the lives and conditions of refugees.
Rescue is one of 15 films shortlisted in the documentary category.
Producers, distributors and other rights holders can submit films for consideration by the European Film Academy. The academy’s board and invited European experts then select films for the shortlist.
Members of the academy, which includes professionals from across the European film industry, watch the shortlisted films and vote to determine the final nominations. They vote again to select the winners once the nominations have been announced.
The final nominations will be announced on November 14. The awards ceremony will take place in Athens, the Greek capital, on January 16.

Liberal Alliance wants mindset interview for citizenship applicant
A debate in Denmark over a proposed law granting citizenship to 2,055 people has centered on whether the applicants have been checked well enough for anti-democratic opinions.
Liberal Alliance, a political party in Denmark, carried out its own check of the people listed in the citizenship bill. During this review, the party found a woman who had repeatedly praised Hamas and former Hamas leaders Yahya Sinwar and Ismail Haniyeh.
Following the discovery, Liberal Alliance wants the woman called in for an interview with Indfødsretsudvalget, the Naturalization Committee of the Danish parliament.
Alex Vanopslagh, the leader of Liberal Alliance, spoke about the matter to the Danish newspaper Politiken.
“As we see it, it just emphasizes the need to wait to grant more citizenships until a proper screening model is in place, so that we can specifically catch some types who, based on what we can see so far, appear strongly anti-democratic,” he told the newspaper.
Every six months, a new bill is introduced in Folketinget, the Danish parliament, to give people Danish citizenship. This happens after an application process that is often long and detailed. This process was also followed under the previous coalition government in Denmark.
The most recent round of citizenships was scheduled at the same time a parliamentary election was called in the spring. Because of the election, the bill that included citizenship for the 2,055 people was delayed.
The delay gave momentum to demands from opposition parties. They argued that officials must carry out a more thorough review of the people on the list to find out if any of them hold anti-democratic views. Socialdemokratiet, the Danish Social Democratic Party, supported this demand as well.
However, the new government decided to present the citizenship bill before a new screening system was ready. This choice led to a larger debate during the opening of the Danish parliament.
During that debate, Rasmus Stoklund, the political spokesperson for Socialdemokratiet, said that if opposition parties found a person on the bill who had anti-democratic views, they could inform the Naturalization Committee. Liberal Alliance has now acted on that suggestion.
Politiken also spoke with the woman identified by the party. She denied that she supports Hamas or any killings.
“I do not support anyone who kills anyone. Because I do not like anyone killing anyone, regardless of whether they are Israeli, Russian or anything else,” the woman told the newspaper.
She stated that she is ready to attend an interview with the committee to explain her position.
Other political parties have reacted differently to the proposal. Dansk Folkeparti, the Danish People’s Party, supports calling the woman in for an interview.
However, Enhedslisten, the Danish left-wing Red-Green Alliance party, strongly opposes the idea.
“It is deeply concerning that Liberal Alliance now to such an extent wants to begin exercising thought control,” Peder Hvelplund, the citizenship spokesperson for Enhedslisten, told Politiken.

The company, which will specialize in combating nationalist crime, will operate using IDF personnel allocations. It began training in August and is expected to take on dedicated operational missions in violence hotspots beginning in late November.
A security official familiar with the training process and operational preparations said, "A Border Police company is like adding two infantry battalions when it comes to nationalist crime. The marginal output of a Border Police company is much higher."
Katz: Israel Police must take full responsibility for nationalist violence in West Bank
Defense Minister Israel Katz said that responsibility for addressing serious violence by a small group of Jewish rioters in the West Bank must rest entirely with the Israel Police's Judea and Samaria Division, including prevention, investigation, and prosecution.
"The IDF should not and cannot engage in civilian law enforcement, but must instead fight Palestinian terrorism and protect the country's borders and Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria and along the seam line," Katz said.
Katz also reiterated that he would not reinstate administrative detention orders.
"Administrative detention orders are not the solution. Only strong and effective police enforcement," he said.
Katz had already announced a proposal in August to transfer authority for handling extremist Jewish activists’ problems from the IDF to the police, which was not coordinated with the relevant authorities and may yet be blocked, The Jerusalem Post learned.
Katz did not clear the issue with a number of top relevant IDF authorities before making the announcement, to the extent that until a meeting on Monday, many of them did not even understand what he was proposing.
New IDF company will be able to respond faster to incidents in West Bank
According to IDF assessments, the new company will be able to respond quickly to incidents of nationalist crime and serve as an operational arm for intelligence gathered by the Israel Police and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency), including in cases of sudden outbreaks of violence.
In August, Zamir ordered the reinforcement of Judea and Samaria with two additional battalions following a sharp increase in the number of isolated farms and new communities in the area, accompanied by growing friction between Israelis and Palestinians, violence, and property damage.
The Judea and Samaria Division currently has four battalions deployed in each of its regional brigades. In addition, a headquarters of the IDF's 98th Division operates in the area to improve oversight, supervision, command, and control, including efforts to prevent nationalist crime.
IDF criticizes police leadership over lack of resources in West Bank
Meanwhile, criticism has emerged within the IDF over the Israel Police's senior leadership, which military officials say has failed to reinforce the Judea and Samaria Police District with additional personnel and resources despite the growing severity of nationalist crime incidents.
A security official noted that the IDF, not the Israel Police, allocates all Border Police positions in Judea and Samaria.
"The Israel Police can strengthen the Judea and Samaria District with more patrol cars and more investigators," the official added.
The IDF has praised the work of Judea and Samaria District commander Moshe Pinchi and the close cooperation between the military and the district. However, military officials maintain that the resources available to the district commander are insufficient.
"This is the smallest district in the police. It is about a third the size of all the other districts in the State of Israel. Why don't they have a special patrol unit to deal with nationalist crime?"

Ra'am, Joint List push community for high voter turnout in hopes of boosting anti-Netanyahu bloc
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19

18:56:32 KST

Israel's Palestinian leaders are urging the Arab community to vote in the October 27 election, hoping that a high turnout could nudge Israel's complex coalition arithmetic in favor of an anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Yashar chairperson Gadi Eisenkot.
"We can ensure the formation of a new government of change," Ra’am head Mansour Abbas told Reuters in his office in Nazareth, Israel's most populous Arab city.
Abbas and other Arab leaders face one big obstacle to their goal of playing a role in any future administration without Netanyahu. Eisenkot has so far ruled out forming a government with the Arab parties that most Palestinian Israelis will vote for, citing a lack of shared values.
But Abbas thinks there will be room to maneuver, perhaps after the vote, largely because of the cold, hard realities of electoral maths.
Recent polls suggest Eisenkot's patchwork bloc of centrist, right- and left-wing parties will get the most votes, but fall short of a majority, and will need Arab support, either as coalition partners or from outside, to prop up a minority government.
"We want to replace the right-wing government... to end the wars and these policies, to stop the expansion of settlements and to address the failure to stop settler attacks," Abbas said.
"We also want a government that brings shared security and peace for Palestinians and Israelis."
For now, Eisenkot is sticking to his position.
“I do not see an Arab party that accepts my principles,” Eisenkot said in a recent interview with The Jerusalem Post, citing, among other issues, their refusal to label Hamas a terrorist organization.
If no bloc forms a workable government, it could lead to a period of political deadlock and then fresh elections in 2027, with Netanyahu left in charge in the meantime.
But Netanyahu, for one, seems to take the threat of some sort of Eisenkot-Arab alliance seriously, or at least sees it as an opportunity to rile up his base. His campaign has used doctored images and AI-generated videos to depict his rivals embracing Arab leaders.
One AI-generated video, released over the summer, showed Eisenkot running through a meadow into the outstretched arms of Abbas.
Abbas' own career shows that such alliances are possible. In 2021 he became the first Arab Muslim to join an Israeli coalition as a minister, in a government led by Naftali Bennett, now a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc.
That government collapsed after 18 months, partly over disagreements between the two men on the West Bank.
This time round, Abbas said he could paper over those differences. To win over Jewish parties, he has taken the unprecedented step of giving the number two spot on his slate to a Jewish former police official, Yoav Segalovitz.
"It sends a message of partnership with the Jewish community and with Jewish citizens," Abbas said.
Arab's frustrated with demonization by Israeli Right, crime
The upcoming election will be Israel’s first since the October 7 massacre, and is being viewed as a referendum on the leadership of Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader.
Abbas' party is projected to win five seats, with a further eight going to the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab parties.
Ahead of the vote, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich proposed a plan to "Judaize" areas around Nazareth in the north and in southern Israel where most Arabs live, describing it as similar to settler expansionism in the West Bank.
Party organizers in Nazareth are hoping to capitalize on Arab anger with Netanyahu, Smotrich and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, as well as frustration with rising crime in their communities.
Last week, canvassers with Abbas' party handed out flyers near Nazareth's massive Church of the Annunciation.
"There is a greater need this time than ever before to go out and vote in large numbers," said one of the people they approached, 74-year-old Gassan Bsoul. "The danger is greater than in the past," he added.
Arab turnout expected to be high
Israeli pollsters expect Arab voter turnout to be higher than in the 2022 and 2020 elections. The Stat-Net Research Institute, based in an Arab Druze town near Haifa, projects turnout at 63%, up from 56% in 2022.
While Abbas has tried to position his party to potentially join government, leaders of the Joint List have said they could wield just as much influence by staying in opposition.
Ahmad Tibi, a Joint List leader, said his group was ready to form "a preventive block to support [a government] from the outside."
He said the Joint List would join an Eisenkot-led government in voting "to establish an official commission of inquiry into October 7," a stated priority of the former military chief and his partners.
"We are placing as our top priority getting rid of the extreme right-wing government of Netanyahu, Smotrich and Ben-Gvir," Tibi said.
Keshet Neev and Shir Perets contributed to this report.

Beyond the Headlines: Dedicating Torah study and why no good deed is done alone - opinion
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:55:52 UTC
18:55:52 KST

One question in the chat caught me by surprise recently. Some 4,000 women had registered for an open class on Parashat Bereishit, organized by the “Mitchadshot” community. At the beginning of the Zoom session, I mentioned that the class was dedicated to the recovery of the students who had been injured in an explosion just hours earlier, during a trip in northern Israel.
Then someone wrote in the chat: “This is my first-ever Torah class. What does it mean to dedicate a class to someone? I’ve never heard of such an idea.”
I explained that every good deed we do in this world generates spiritual merits. Torah study and prayer have a special spiritual power. And when we do something good, we can dedicate the merit of that act to a particular purpose. For example, to the recovery of someone who was injured just hours earlier.
The Jewish people are bound together by a sense of mutual responsibility. We all affect one another through our good deeds and mitzvot - or, God forbid, through our wrongdoing. We are all part of one human fabric, and every action has an impact.
Then, just as the Zoom class was ending, almost as though it were a direct continuation of our discussion, I received a message written by Chani Leiter, the mother of Neria, who was seriously wounded in a terrorist attack several weeks ago:
Mutual responsibility, Jewish concern extends beyond the personal
“From the intensive care unit at Shaare Zedek Medical Center, we are receiving messages and videos of so many prayers, Torah study, acts of kindness, and good deeds being performed all around the world on behalf of our Neria. If only I could describe how much strength this gives us.
“We are seeing how the mutual responsibility and concern of the Jewish people extend far beyond our own personal ordeal. This is the hidden Jewish soul, now revealing itself.
“We named our son Neria - the light of God - because we wanted him to spread God's light in the world. God's ways are mysterious, but we can see with our own eyes how Neria is doing exactly that right now. All of this surrounds us with love and gives us strength.”
Wow.
A question from one woman and an answer from one mother remind us of something fundamental: No one is ever alone, and no good deed benefits only the person who performs it.
May Neria Dov ben Chana, and all those who were injured, have a complete and speedy recovery.
If Not Now, When?
When Sandy and Rosalie Goldstein were in their forties, they were both considering making Aliyah from the United States. Somehow, after a conversation with an official, they mistakenly received the impression that they were too old. They understood that Sandy would not be able to find work in Israel as an accountant at his age, and so they put the dream aside and continued building their lives in New Jersey.
Decades passed. But it is always possible to grow, to renew ourselves, to do better. And today, you can find the Goldsteins in Netanya, surrounded by grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Some members of the family had already made aliyah before them, and they themselves are just one small part of the worldwide wave of aliyah.
You look at their ID cards, and you cannot help but be inspired. Sandy has just celebrated his 105th birthday, and Rosalie will turn 101 in January. This month, they will celebrate their 79th (!) wedding anniversary.
They could have stayed in their comfort zone. They had already built careers in the United States, raised a family, worked on behalf of Soviet Jews behind the Iron Curtain, and over the years had also grown stronger in their observance of Torah and mitzvot.
They both love to quote the ancient words of Hillel the Elder: “If not now, when?”
They remind us: whatever change or improvement we have been dreaming about, whatever new beginning we have been postponing - now is the time.
5 Things About the Parashah
1. This week’s Torah portion, Lech Lecha, is the third portion in the Torah. In a sense, we are starting from the beginning for the third time. The universal, global “experiments” of the Garden of Eden, Noah’s Ark, and the Tower of Babel have all failed. The world needs nations, countries, and distinct identities. The world needs Avraham.
2. Avraham and Sarah make their first appearance on the stage of history - and, in fact, have never left it. If there were a ranking of the most influential people in human history, they would take first place. Billions of people around the world consider themselves their spiritual heirs.
3. Avraham and Sarah are the first olim, the first immigrants to the Land of Israel. “Go forth from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father’s house,” God tells Avraham - and he sets out for the Land of Israel. Millions have followed in his footsteps over the generations.
4. The first commandment Avraham fulfills is also the only commandment in this Torah portion: brit milah, circumcision. Close to 100 percent of his Jewish descendants continue to observe it to this day.
5. It’s worth remembering: In his own time, nobody called him our forefather Avraham. They probably called him Avraham the eccentric, the lunatic. The entire world worshipped idols, while he introduced us to the revolutionary ideas of monotheism, charity and kindness, faith and optimism. Today, everyone knows he was right.

Unknown Publisher

18:55:21 KST

Approximately 60,000 children in the Gaza Strip have lost one or both parents during the war, according to the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), which warned of the lasting psychological and humanitarian consequences for children affected by the conflict.
Speaking at a press briefing at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, UNICEF communications officer and deputy spokesperson Riccardo Pires said around 800,000 children remain displaced, with most living in tents or damaged buildings considered unsafe.
Pires said nearly all displaced children require some form of mental health and psychosocial support to help them cope with the trauma of the war.
He also reported that more than 340 children have been killed and hundreds injured in Gaza since the ceasefire was declared in October 2025.
The UNICEF official warned that overcrowding in displacement areas, inadequate sanitation and deteriorating living conditions continue to expose children and their families to serious health and safety risks, particularly as winter approaches.
READ: Gaza buries remains of 75 Palestinians recovered from rubble of homes destroyed by Israel
Despite these challenges, Pires said the ceasefire had facilitated increased deliveries of humanitarian aid and commercial supplies, contributing to improvements in food security.
He also noted progress in restoring access to education, reporting that more than 560,000 children have returned to learning, including those attending classes at over 200 UNICEF-supported learning centers.
However, Pires expressed concern about the deterioration of Gaza’s sanitation infrastructure, warning that all six wastewater treatment plants remain out of service.
As a result, he said, much of the territory’s untreated sewage is being discharged directly into the sea, posing additional environmental and public health risks.
UNICEF stressed that continued displacement, damaged infrastructure and the approaching winter threaten to deepen the humanitarian crisis facing Gaza’s children, despite improvements in aid deliveries and educational access.

18:55:00 KST

Residents of the oil-rich province of Alberta vote Monday in a referendum on whether to stay in Canada or start a process toward a legally binding secession vote.
Recent polls show about 70% of residents favor remaining part of Canada, while roughly 20% favor secession and the remainder are undecided.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and both of the country's major political parties have repeatedly opposed secession. Support for the independence movement has also come from former U.S. President Donald Trump.
Alberta, a province of about 5 million people, has about 3.1 million eligible voters, according to Elections Alberta, the province's election authority.
Polls open at 9 a.m. (3 p.m. GMT) and close at 6 p.m., though advance postal and in-person voting has already taken place.
Voters will decide 10 questions. The secession question will be counted first. Results could be available as early as Tuesday, according to election officials.
Calgary, with about 1.68 million residents, is Alberta's largest city, followed by the capital, Edmonton, with about 1.28 million. Its national parks in the Rocky Mountains attract tourists worldwide.
Alberta has some of Canada's most conservative voters. A movement advocating independence on cultural and economic grounds has existed for years.
Some oil industry representatives feel environmental regulations restrict them, while many protesters who opposed coronavirus restrictions and vaccine mandates later joined the independence movement.
Although the movement has long represented a minority of Albertans, it persuaded Smith, the province's conservative premier, to call the referendum. Smith herself has consistently advocated remaining part of Canada.

WFP cuts Gaza aid for 500,000 people as Israeli restrictions strain food supplies
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:52:53 UTC
18:52:53 KST

The UN World Food Programme (WFP) announced on Monday that funding shortages have forced it to cut food assistance in Gaza by around one-third, leaving half a million people without critical support as winter approaches.
In a statement, the agency said it is now assisting 1.1 million vulnerable people in Gaza, down from 1.6 million last month, while food rations have been halved.
Families receiving assistance will now get one food parcel instead of two, along with a smaller bag of wheat flour, it said.
The number of daily hot meals has also dropped from 250,000 to 150,000, while families in hard-to-reach areas, including near the Israeli army-controlled "yellow line," will receive meals every other day instead of daily.
The agency has also reduced the value of cash assistance for 75,000 families.
According to WFP, an estimated 1.4 million people, or 67 percent of Gaza's population, face crisis-level food insecurity or worse, including around 200,000 experiencing emergency conditions requiring immediate food assistance to prevent deaths from hunger.
Only one in five children consumes a sufficiently diverse diet, while unemployment exceeds 80 percent, leaving many families unable to afford nutritious food.
Israeli restrictions further strain food supplies
Israeli restrictions on aid deliveries and commercial imports have further strained food supplies in Gaza, compounding the impact of WFP’s funding shortfall.
In July, the UN humanitarian office, OCHA, reported that only 42 percent of aid arriving via Egypt and 65 percent of shipments from Ashdod port could be offloaded at Kerem Shalom in one week.
WFP has also said more than 70 percent of Gaza’s cropland is inaccessible, with only about 3 percent currently usable, limiting local food production.
The suspension of commercial shipments last week has added to the pressure.
On October 14, COGAT, the Israeli military body overseeing humanitarian affairs, announced that commercial goods would no longer enter Gaza, cutting off a major source of perishable foods, including fruit and meat, which aid agencies typically do not supply.
WFP warned that "modest" improvements in food security since the October 2025 ceasefire remain "fragile" and could quickly be reversed by further reductions in humanitarian assistance.
Funding shortages have also forced the agency to halve its assistance in the occupied West Bank, from 400,000 to 200,000 people.
The agency said it urgently needs $450 million to sustain critical operations across Gaza and the West Bank over the next six months, through March 2027.

“Russia’s response, time and again, has been ballistic missiles, ‘shaheds’ and killings,” Zelensky said.

Kaohsiung completes flood control checks ahead of Typhoon Champi
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:49:31 UTC
18:49:31 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Kaohsiung has completed preparations and tests for its flood control facilities ahead of Typhoon Champi, which could bring strong winds and heavy rain later this week, the city’s Water Resources Bureau said Monday.
The Central Weather Administration forecast the storm will move northwest over waters east of Taiwan, with its greatest impact on Kaohsiung expected on Friday and Saturday, per CNA. Its outer circulation could bring intense short-duration rainfall, increasing flood risks.
All 100 pumping stations, 148 mobile pumps, and 29 detention ponds have completed operational tests, the bureau said. Emergency supplies and emergency personnel are ready for deployment, while staff monitor the typhoon’s path and debris flow risks in mountainous areas, it added.
The bureau has intensified inspections and clearing of drainage channels and stormwater sewers. Additional desilting has been completed at sites affected by sediment buildup during August’s heavy rains, including Houjing Creek in Renwu District.
The city’s 29 detention ponds have a combined capacity of 5.59 million metric tons, per CNA. Depending on forecasts and real-time water levels, the bureau will lower pond levels in advance to make room for incoming rainwater.
The bureau will use its smart water management system to monitor rainfall and water levels. It urged residents to follow typhoon updates and prepare flood barriers or sandbags in low-lying areas.

Keiji Furuya, a member of Japan’s House of Representatives, called the policy shift an important step in Taiwan-Japan relations. He said lawmakers would continue working toward allowing all Taiwanese residents to list “Taiwan” on their national certifications.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) faces opposition to his proposal to relocate Songshan Airport and redevelop the site as an AI park, with a recent poll showing more residents oppose the plan than support it.
A TVBS poll released Saturday found that 41% of Taipei residents opposed the proposal, compared with 31% who supported it, while 28% expressed no opinion. The survey interviewed 1,131 Taipei adults from Monday to Thursday and had a reported margin of error of plus or minus 2.9%, per TVBS.
At the opening of the Lihu Childcare Center on Monday, Chiang said he was willing to listen to views from all sectors and work with the central government to resolve difficulties associated with relocating the airport, per CNA.
Chiang said Terminal 3 at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport, scheduled to open in 2027, and its third runway, planned for 2033, could help accommodate flights currently handled by Songshan Airport. He said the period between 2027 and 2033 could be used to review the necessary arrangements and prepare for future industrial development.
The proposal has drawn scrutiny from the central government. Cabinet Secretary-General Chang Tun-han (張惇涵) said relocating Songshan Airport could not be decided by a few people looking at PowerPoint presentations, underscoring the need for a more detailed review.
Chiang responded that the Taipei City Government had informed the central government in 2023 that relocating the airport would benefit the city’s long-term development. He added that the city began coordinating with the Ministry of National Defense in 2024 over the recovery of land at Songnan Military Camp to develop an AI industrial cluster.
The mayor has proposed transforming about 300 hectares of airport land and surrounding areas into an AI park incorporating technology businesses, residential communities, and green space.
Transportation is a point of contention. Chiang said Sunday that business travelers could reach Taipei from Taoyuan Airport in about 36 minutes using the airport MRT or elevated highways, per CNA.
DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) said the proposal did not yet provide a complete alternative to Songshan Airport. Opposition has also come from outside politics. Pegatron Chair Tung Tzu-hsien (童子賢) said relocating the airport was inadvisable, arguing that a capital should retain a regional air transport hub, per UDN.

India: End the crackdown on peaceful protests and release arbitrarily detained protesters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:48:34 UTC
18:48:34 KST

The brutal crackdown on peaceful protesters in New Delhi over the last weekend is alarming with mass detention, unlawful use of force, the targeting of journalists, human rights defenders including lawyers, and internet shutdowns, said rights groups in a statement.
Amnesty International, CIVICUS, Front Line Defenders and South Asians for Human Rights call on the Indian authorities to release everyone arbitrarily detained for the exercise of their right to freedom of peaceful assembly and ensure accountability for abuses by security forces.
On 10 October 2026, protests were called by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and backed by student groups calling for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of India, following reports that the nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls by the election commission removed around 130 million names from voter lists.
Since the call for protests, authorities used Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to ban gatherings of more than five people. Ahead of the 10 October protest, more than 50,000 police and security personnel were reportedly deployed, some drawn from other states. Trains and buses to New Delhi were cancelled or suspended, metro train stations were closed, and the city’s borders were sealed to large vehicles. Anti-riot vehicles with tear gas launchers were stationed near protest sites.
At least 10,000 people were reportedly detained for violating prohibitory orders across India before the march, many while travelling to Delhi. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and other leaders were detained for violating prohibitory orders on 10 October after landing at Delhi airport and were held overnight. Thousands of protesters were arbitrarily detained by the police in New Delhi including journalists who were covering the protests. Others detained included student leader Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and economist Jean Drèze.
Police moved to break up the demonstrations before they could begin, intercepting demonstrators on their way to Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in central Delhi. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centres. Some police personnel had no visible name tags.
Arbitrary detentions continued on 11 October and there were reports of physical attacks by police on protesters in detention. Many women protesters and journalists accused security personnel of sexual harassment while detaining them during the protests.
Right-wing vigilante groups were also seen threatening and assaulting protesters and journalists. Some of them harassed Muslim women journalists while they were covering the protests.
Nearly 40 journalists were detained over the two days. Some of them were physically assaulted, intimidated, and had their camera and mobile phones seized or destroyed despite showing their press identity cards.
A group of lawyers who carried out a rally near the Supreme Court in support of protesters also faced unlawful force by police and some were detained briefly.
Instagram accounts of the news outlets Molitics and Journo Mirror have been blocked in India during its coverage of the protests citing Information Technology Rules.
On 10 October authorities also ordered a 24-hour mobile internet shutdown in central Delhi. Mobile internet was also reportedly blocked at eight stadiums used as detention centres, cutting detainees off from their lawyers and families. Reports also suggest that the shutdown was taking place beyond areas of protests and detention.
On 13 October, the Delhi Police de-notified the Jantar Mantar area in central Delhi as a protest spot and provided alternative venues further away. CJP leaders continued their protest and were arrested near Jantar Mantar. On 14 October Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from CJP were ordered by a court to be detained in judicial custody for five-days for ‘trespassing’ in Jantar Mantar.
The right to protest is protected in India’s constitution. Demonstrations should not depend on obtaining prior permission from the police. At most, organizers may be expected to notify the authorities of their plans.
The crackdown follows the July 2026 CJP protests where human rights groups documented unlawful use of force against those protests, including pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas and no officer in Delhi Police has been held accountable.
We call on the Indian authorities to:
- Immediately and unconditionally release all those detained solely for exercising their right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and drop all charges against protesters, journalists and lawyers who have been arbitrarily detained
- Undertake an independent investigation of violations committed by security forces against protesters, activists and journalists including arbitrary detention, unnecessary and excessive force, ill-treatment and sexual harassment and bring those responsible to account
- Instruct all police and security personnel to respect journalists’ right to report, return seized or damaged equipment, and stop coercing journalists to delete footage or hand over personal data
- End arbitrary internet shutdowns and the blocking of accounts that cover or support protests
- Ensure that all uniformed law enforcement officials conducting policing of demonstrations must wear identity badges in visible places
- Investigate and prosecute violence by non-state actors against protesters and journalists
- Ensure that security forces follow the UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials while responding to peaceful protests
- Ensure peaceful protesters are able to demand accountability from those in power without facing intimidation, arbitrary detention, or sweeping restrictions on their freedoms.
Signed,
Amnesty International
CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
Front Line Defenders
South Asians for Human Rights (SAHR)

The International Food Exhibition Kicks Off in Paris
Italy
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
11:45:59 CEST
18:45:59 KST

The 2026 edition of SIAL Paris was inaugurated yesterday in Paris at the Paris Nord Villepinte exhibition center, the International Food Exhibition, in the presence of Annie Genevard, French Minister of Agriculture, Agri-Food, and Food Sovereignty, and representatives from the Italian Embassy in France. The event, scheduled to run through October 21, sees Italy once again take the lead in terms of exhibition space, with a total of approximately 700 companies participating in the fair. As part of the Italian delegation, ICE Agenzia is organizing a collective exhibition featuring 218 companies spread across Halls 1, 5B, and 7, covering a total area of approximately 3,000 m². The Italian presence offers companies an important opportunity to showcase their products of excellence to international operators and develop new business relationships with buyers, importers, and distributors.
                                    
The French market plays a leading role for the Italian agri-food sector. In fact, France is the sector’s second-largest export destination, after Germany. In 2025—the year in which Italian agri-food exports exceeded 72 billion euros worldwide—French imports of agri-food products from Italy reached 6.84 billion euros, marking a 4.78% increase compared to 2024. This positive trend continued in the first half of 2026: the value of French imports from Italy stood at 3.35 billion euros, up 2.3% compared to the same period the previous year.
                                    
The breakdown of this trade highlights the diversity of Italian production. In the first six months of 2026, French imports of Italian cheeses reached 563.7 million euros (+1.8%), those of pasta 254.7 million (+0.4%), and those of hams and cured meats 107.4 million (+5%). At SIAL, the member companies of the collective will showcase this diversity of supply chains: Hall 1 will feature gourmet specialties, Hall 5B will showcase confectionery products, and Hall 7 will highlight dairy products. For industry professionals, this will be an opportunity to meet directly with companies from different regions, all united by a focus on quality, product origin, and innovation. Participation in SIAL Paris 2026 confirms the trade show’s strategic role as an international hub for promoting the Italian agri-food sector. In France, Italy’s second-largest export market, exports reached 6.7 billion euros, up more than 5% from the previous year. Against the backdrop of slowing growth in 2026, SIAL represents a crucial opportunity to consolidate the results achieved and open up new opportunities in international markets. The Italian pavilion was inaugurated today in the presence of ICE Agency President Matteo Zoppas, who, at the conclusion of the ceremony, met with representatives from the Italian regions in attendance, the companies participating in the collective exhibition, and the main industry associations. Among the institutional guests who graced the opening ceremony were Nicola Caputo, Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Antonio Tajani, responsible for exports and the internationalization of the agri-food sector; and Fabio Cannavaro, Ambassador of Serie A, whose presence helped strengthen the link between the excellence of “Made in Italy,” the international promotion of Italy’s image, and the great ambassadors of Italian sports around the world.
                                    
During the event, the Italian pavilion will today welcome Luigi D’Eramo, Undersecretary of State at the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty, and Forests (MASAF), who is in Paris for the Ministerial Conference on Agriculture. The visit will provide an important opportunity to engage with Italian companies participating in SIAL and to highlight the quality and competitiveness of the national agri-food sector in international markets.

Indonesia fires ‘have burned nearly 2 mln hectares’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:45:55 UTC
18:45:55 KST

Members of the all-women The Power of Mama (TPoM) volunteer firefighting team spray water onto smouldering peatland in Mensubuk Lama, Tanjungpura Village, Ketapang Regency, West Kalimantan on September 26, 2026. (AFP File Photo)
Fires in Indonesia burned through over 1.9 million hectares between January and the end of September this year, a monitor analyzing satellite imagery said on Oct. 19.
The figure, an area nearly 12 times larger than London, is a conservative estimate in part because haze has complicated satellite verification, said David Gaveau, founder of deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas.
Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July.
Gaveau said the true scale of the burning was likely to be even higher than the 1,916,588 hectares his organization has detected so far.
“Our burned-area estimates are conservative for two reasons. First, we exclude individual burn scars smaller than 6.25 hectares. Second, we prioritize avoiding false detections,” he said.
This year, the calculation has also been impacted by heavy haze, which has obscured satellite images at times.
“The total reported burned area therefore underestimates the true area burned,” he said.
Even so, Nusantara Atlas data shows the area burned by the end of September this year was 38 percent higher than the same point in 2019.
The satellites the monitor uses were not available during severe fires in 2015, so comparable data is not available.

Russian Satellite Kosmos-2612 Closes to Within 26 Meters of ICEYE-X36 During Pursuit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:45:11 UTC
18:45:11 KST

Russia’s military satellite Kosmos-2612 is reportedly pursuing ICEYE-X36, a commercial radar satellite, and has approached it to within 26 meters.
This is evidenced by data from the monitoring service satellitemap.space, which was analyzed by Militarnyi.
ICEYE-X36 is operated by Finnish company ICEYE, which cooperates with Ukraine and provides satellite imagery for intelligence and reconnaissance.
As of 02:06 UTC on October 19, Kosmos-2612 was approximately 640 meters behind ICEYE-X36 and 2 kilometers above it. Later, at 16:07 UTC, the distance between the two satellites narrowed to just 26 meters.
According to the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), Kosmos-2612 began a series of maneuvers in late September 2026 that allowed it to enter the same orbital plane as ICEYE-X36 and approach its altitude.
On October 12, the Russian satellite performed a maneuver that changed its velocity by about 27.9 m/s, adjusting its orbit to an altitude of around 555 km, nearly the same as ICEYE-X36.
Currently, the Russian satellite orbits at 557.5 km, while ICEYE-X36 orbits at 554.7 km.
Such maneuvers require significant fuel, as changing a satellite’s orbital inclination requires a substantial velocity adjustment.
However, once a satellite reaches the same orbital plane as another, it can approach that satellite while using less fuel for subsequent orbital adjustments.
This allows the satellite to approach its target for close observation, structural inspection, or potential interference with its operations.
Militarnyi previously reported that on April 17, 2026, Russia launched a Soyuz-2.1b carrier rocket from the Plesetsk military cosmodrome, carrying a classified payload for the Russian Ministry of Defense.
After placing the satellites into orbit, one was designated Kosmos-2612.

Swiss security firm accused of thousands of labour law breaches
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
09:44:24 UTC
18:44:24 KST

Swiss security firm accused of thousands of labour law breaches
Securitas, a Swiss company operating in the security services market, is alleged to have forced employees to work many excessively long shifts for years.
Some experts have told the Swiss public broadcaster SRF that the group’s practices constitute systematic breaches of labour law.
According to an analysis of internal data carried out by SRF Investigativ, SRF’s investigative journalism unit, there were reportedly around 20,000 breaches of the Labour Act between 2023 and 2025.
Around 900 employees are said to have been affected. The main issues are reported to have been excessively long shifts and insufficient rest periods. Staff concerned are said to have been employed in prisons, hospitals and asylum seeker centres.
All of this “is a sign of systematic practice”, Denis G. Humbert, a lawyer specialising in labour law, told SRF, calling for the authorities to intervene. “It is not permissible, it is unacceptable. This constitutes the exploitation of staff and is not allowed.”
Kurt Pärli, a professor of law at the University of Basel, echoed this view. Wat has come to light “cannot be explained away as a simple planning error. The problem with this situation goes far beyond that”.
Securitas has issued a written statement admitting that, in some cases, the practices adopted did not comply with the principles of labour law or the company’s values.
Measures taken in recent years have led to a reduction in problematic cases. The company disputes the total figure of 20,000 breaches.
While not ruling out the possibility of errors, the company said that there has been no general and systematic breach of the Labour Act.

Police investigate Grolsch beer tasting contamination

Unknown Publisher

09:41:35 UTC

Police investigate Grolsch beer tasting contamination
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Eleven people fell ill on Saturday afternoon after tasting water during a tour of the Grolsch brewery in Enschede. The water may have been contaminated with caustic soda, according to local broadcaster RTV Oost.
The group of nine visitors and two guides had been given shot glasses of the spring water used to brew the beer, a tasting that has been part of the tour for years.
One of the victims told RTV Oost that several people noticed a strange, sour taste and a burning feeling in their stomach after drinking it. Members of the group became nauseous and vomited, and the broadcaster said they may have suffered internal burns to the throat, oesophagus and stomach.
Several ambulances went to the brewery, and a German trauma team was called out but turned out not to be needed. All 11 were out of hospital on Sunday, and one spent the night in hospital, Grolsch told public broadcaster NOS.
Police have started a forensic investigation, and the labour inspectorate is also investigating. A police spokesperson told NOS it could have been an accident, “or something else could be going on”.
Grolsch said the tap the group drank from is separate from the rest of the production process, and that the quality and safety of its beer “are not and have not been at risk”. The company said it would not comment on possible causes while the investigation is ongoing.

SEOUL, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Monday reaffirmed his firm commitment to the early recovery of South Korea's wartime operational control (OPCON) from the United States.
Lee said during a press conference that Seoul must and definitely can retrieve it ahead of schedule, saying that the term "transfer" regarding OPCON, which had been used previously, should be changed to terms such as recovery or retrieval.
Lee underscored that military sovereignty is one of the most critical core components of national sovereignty, saying OPCON must be recovered swiftly to meet the minimum requirements of a sovereign state.
Expressing his firm confidence in the independent defense capabilities of the South Korean military, Lee said South Korea should and is fully capable of handling its own defense.
In the early 1950s, South Korea handed over command of its military to the U.S.-led "United Nations Command." In 1978, it was then transferred to the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, which is headed by a U.S. military officer. South Korea retook peacetime operational control of its forces in 1994, but has not yet regained wartime operational control. ■

NAGOYA, Japan, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Powerlifter Cui Zhe led from her opening attempt to win the women's 41kg title at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games on Monday, delivering China's first gold medal of the Games.
"This is my fifth Asian Para Games, and I'm so happy to win the first gold for China today," Cui said. "I want to thank my country, our coaching team and everyone back home who has supported me."
Cui also won China's first gold medal at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, where she claimed the women's 41kg title with a decisive final lift. Eight years later and less than two months shy of her 40th birthday, she opened Monday's competition with a confident 110kg lift, immediately putting herself 10kg ahead of nearest rival Tursynay Kabyl of Kazakhstan.
Cui extended her lead with a 115kg second lift. When Kabyl, the penultimate lifter, selected 104kg for her third attempt, Cui's gold was secured. The champion was not finished, however. She called for 120kg on her final attempt and completed the lift cleanly, surpassing the personal best of 119kg she set at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games. After the lift was declared good, Cui turned to the crowd, waved and smiled broadly.
"I focused on staying calm because I had never lifted that weight in competition. I just wanted to get every detail right," she said.
Cui's victory extended a remarkable streak, as she has competed at all five editions of the Asian Para Games and won gold at each one. A Paralympic veteran since Beijing 2008, she finally claimed Paralympic gold in Paris in 2024.
Looking ahead, Cui sees Nagoya as part of her build-up to Los Angeles 2028. "I view this as a test on the road to the 2028 Paralympics. I hope I can lift even better there," she said.
Earlier on Monday, China's Chen Liuxun secured the delegation's first medal of the Games, taking bronze in the men's 49kg para powerlifting with a best lift of 161kg. ■

China's innovation-related investment holds steady despite broader fixed-asset decline
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
17:38:49 CST
18:38:49 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's investment in innovation-driven sectors held up well in the first three quarters of 2026, even as overall fixed-asset investment continued to contract, official data showed on Monday.
Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.3 percent year on year in the Jan.-Sept. period, while investment in high-tech industries grew 4.9 percent, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said in a statement.
Notably, several sectors posted particularly strong gains. Investment in information services surged 20.2 percent from a year earlier, and aerospace equipment manufacturing investment climbed 12.5 percent, while investment in electronic and communications equipment manufacturing rose 7.6 percent.
The resilience of these sectors stands in contrast to the broader investment picture. Total fixed-asset investment fell 7.2 percent year on year to 33.41 trillion yuan (4.97 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first three quarters of 2026, dragged down in part by a slump in real estate investment. Excluding real estate development investment, total fixed-asset investment declined 4.2 percent.
In breakdown, infrastructure investment fell 4.2 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, manufacturing investment dropped 2.1 percent, and real estate development investment declined 20.6 percent in this period. Private sector investment, meanwhile, contracted by 10.4 percent.
While overall growth has slowed, investment is playing an increasingly important role in optimizing supply and driving innovation, Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS, told a press conference on Monday.
Analysts said the current pullback in overall investment reflects a transition from a traditional investment model to a new one.
"Investment is undergoing a profound shift in emphasis from traditional sectors to emerging ones, and from scale expansion to efficiency improvement," said Liu Yuanchun, president of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.
China's effective investment space remains vast over the medium and long term, Liu said, noting that artificial intelligence (AI) and new infrastructure will serve as key engines for the next round of effective investment.
The expansion of AI applications is spurring sustained investment across industrial chains.
NBS data revealed that in the first three quarters of 2026, investment in electronic circuit manufacturing surged 58.7 percent year on year, and integrated circuit manufacturing investment rose 14.2 percent. Meanwhile, companies are accelerating their shift toward intelligent operations, driving a 9.7 percent increase in investment in equipment and tools purchases.
In terms of new infrastructure, China's "six networks" initiative, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks, represents a major investment opportunity. It is estimated that investment in these six networks and related areas will exceed 7 trillion yuan in 2026.
Investment will increasingly serve the development of new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system, with the ultimate results felt in expanded employment, rising incomes and improved living standards, Liu said. ■

China's industrial growth gains momentum in first three quarters as new growth drivers expand
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-19
17:38:44 CST
18:38:44 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's industrial sector continued to gain momentum in the first three quarters of 2026, with high-tech and equipment manufacturing expanding rapidly, official data showed Monday.
The country's value-added industrial output increased by 5.3 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, accelerating by 0.3 percentage points from August, the data showed.
Despite a complex environment, China's industrial sector maintained steady growth and made further progress in the first three quarters, Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS, said at a press conference.
NBS data showed value-added output of equipment manufacturing grew 10.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, while high-tech manufacturing rose 14.3 percent. Both outpaced overall industrial growth by 4.9 and 9 percentage points, respectively.
Equipment and high-tech manufacturing accounted for 37.6 percent and 18.3 percent of value-added industrial output during the period, respectively, Mao said, describing them as key drivers of industrial transformation and high-quality development.
Industrial output is used to measure the activity of large enterprises each with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.98 million U.S. dollars).
At the product level, output of industrial robots jumped 29.1 percent year on year, while 3D printing equipment and lithium-ion batteries saw increases of 62.5 percent and 39.5 percent, respectively.
New growth drivers, represented by high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy, and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first nine months, Mao said, citing preliminary estimates.
"The baton of economic growth is being passed increasingly to new growth drivers," he said.
The figures reflect China's broader push to upgrade its industrial structure and cultivate new growth drivers. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) underscores the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as its backbone.
Earlier this month, China issued guidelines to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces. The measures include advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, and innovating development approaches.
Overall, China's economy remained generally stable in the first three quarters, with new growth drivers gaining strength and the economic structure continuing to improve, Mao said. ■

BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's job market remained generally stable in the first three quarters of 2026, with the surveyed urban unemployment rate declining in September, official data showed on Monday.
The average surveyed urban unemployment rate stood at 5.2 percent in the first nine months of the year, unchanged from the same period of 2025, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).
In September alone, the surveyed urban unemployment rate came in at 5.2 percent, down 0.1 percentage points from the previous month.
The surveyed unemployment rate among workers with local household registration was 5.2 percent, while that among workers with non-local household registration stood at 5.1 percent. The rate for migrant workers with rural household registration was 5.0 percent.
The services sector remained a main driver of employment, accounting for 49.4 percent of the country's total workforce. Employment increased in sectors including transportation, accommodation and catering, as well as culture, sports and entertainment, according to Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS.
Since the beginning of the year, China has introduced a series of policies to boost employment, with a target to keep the surveyed urban unemployment rate around 5.5 percent in 2026 and create more than 12 million new urban jobs during the year.
China released a five-year plan on human resources and social security development in July. Among other targets for the 2026-2030 period, the plan aims to help 25 million unemployed urban workers find new jobs and provide employment assistance to 6.5 million people having difficulty finding work.
The country is also stepping up efforts to adapt its labor market to rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI), seeking to harness technological innovation to create jobs while addressing its impact on employment.
A five-year plan on implementing the employment-first strategy identified promoting employment amid AI advances as a key task, calling for creating jobs through AI applications and tapping the potential in traditional sectors. ■

NAIROBI, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Kenya's health authorities have confirmed an eighth Ebola case after a 49-year-old patient attendant tested positive.
Patrick Amoth, director-general for health in the Ministry of Health, confirmed the patient attendant is in isolation, adding that existing patients are showing positive recovery.
Amoth added that 38 people were tested on Sunday, with one coming positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.
The eighth case is a 49-year-old man who developed fever, headache and muscle pain, Amoth said during an interview with Kenya's Citizen TV.
The health official said the patient had been isolated as health officials prepared to begin treatment.
He said all seven previously confirmed patients had received monoclonal antibodies, adding that those who had undergone the treatment were responding well.
"All of them, I can confirm categorically, have received monoclonal antibodies," he said.
There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the Kenyan outbreak, although candidate products are being evaluated in clinical trials, according to the World Health Organization.
The new case comes after the country announced four new Ebola cases on Saturday, including a close male relative of the country's first patient and three health workers who attended to him while he was in hospital.
Amoth further allayed fears of community transmission, saying there was a low possibility that the quarantined persons transmitted the disease at community level.
According to the Ministry of Health, authorities have actively traced contacts and placed individuals exposed to confirmed cases under quarantine.
As of Oct. 17, health officials had identified 130 contacts of the first patient and traced 128 of them, the Ministry of Health said. Contact tracing for the cases confirmed since then is continuing.
Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case on Oct. 6. The index patient, a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), arrived in Nairobi on Oct. 3.
The patient died while undergoing treatment at a Nairobi hospital and was later accorded a safe and dignified burial at a public cemetery to minimize the risk of transmission. ■

"Seven people were killed, 17 injured, and eight suffered amputations due to landmine and explosive remnants of war (ERW) explosions so far this year," he told Xinhua.

To tackle the ongoing threat, Cambodia launched a new National Mine Action Policy last month, pushing its target to eliminate all identified landmines, cluster bombs, and ERWs by 2035. ■
